newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN NEUHAUS IPO PRICED AT 1,600 TO 1,750 BFR.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN NEUHAUS IPO PRICED AT 1,600 TO 1,750 BFR.

text.p: Shares in the initial public offering by Belgian luxury chocolate maker Neuhaus NV will be priced between 1,600 and 1,750 Belgian francs, lead managers Petercam SA said on Wednesday.

Institutional investors will be able to subscribe from February 20. On February 27 the final price wil be set and the offer will be opened to the public. It is planned the shares will begin trading on the Brussels Stock Exchange on March 10.
"The price will be a maximum 1,750 francs," Petercam manager Pierre Drion told a news conference.
Controlling shareholder Artal Nederland BV, a holding company representing the interests of two Belgian families, has applied to list 750,000 shares on the bourse.
Sixty percent, or 450,000 shares, is being offered for sale in the IPO, of which two thirds is intended for institutions.

Petercam said the exact allotment to institutional and retail investors could change as a function of demand. It has a "green shoe" agreement with Artal to buy, if needed, a further six percent, or 45,000 shares, to sell to the market in the aftermath of the listing.
Drion said using a dividend discount model, Neuhaus shares were valued at 1,761 francs, giving a market capitalisation of 1.32 billion Belgian francs.

At 1,750 francs, Neuhaus is expected to have a 1996/97 price earnings ratio of 16.5, yielding 3.8 percent. Current earnings, excluding amortization of goodwill, are expected to grow 33 percent in 1996/97 to 80 million francs, or 106 francs a share.
The shares sold will be eligible for dividends from the financial year ending June 30, 1997.
Petercam said Neuhaus's projected market ratios compared favourably with those of similar listed companies.
Belgian biscuit company Corona-Lotus has a 1996 P/E of around 17.3. British luxury chocolate group Thorntons was presently trading around 22.5 times earnings.
Full details of the offer and prospectus are available on Petercam's web site at: http://www.petercam.be.
